tasks.task: Write a tailored demo script from discovery notes

items.when: When discovery notes exist and the demo must answer this buyer's problems in their order
When the deal reaches technical evaluation and the demo is the first of several steps
Before scripting, to outline how belief builds and where you ask for the next step
When you want a second shape to try: explain briefly, then let the buyer see the result themselves
When the script is drafted, to find the flat stretches where the room stops watching
Before the demo, to read the script as the buyer's IT lead with their notes in hand
When a step only makes sense if you already know the product

tasks.task: Check discovery is good enough before building a demo

items.when: When a demo is booked and you want to know if you can tailor it or must ask more first
When gaps are found and you need the questions to send or ask before the demo
When you do not know who will be in the room or who signs off the technical choice
When there is one more call before the demo and it should build on the last call's notes
When the notes list what the buyer wants and nothing on what the problem costs them

tasks.task: Write the same-day demo follow-up email

items.when: Straight after a demo, to recap what they saw against their problems and lock the next step
When you have the transcript and also need the team summary and CRM updates
When the email should carry a dated plan from here to a decision
When you want a version where the buyer can say no and the deal still moves
Before sending, to cut it and check open questions each have an owner

tasks.task: Write a pilot or proof-of-concept plan with success measures

items.when: When the buyer wants a pilot and it must end in a clear yes or no on agreed measures
Before the plan, to score the buyer's requirements for gaps and set out the trial
When the pilot could be narrow and fast or broad and slow, to show both with cost and dates
When one success measure needs a clean test that says what each result means
When the plan looks sound, to hear the best case that the pilot will prove nothing

tasks.task: Track a running pilot and the promises made in it

items.when: When weekly check-ins must report against the measures agreed at the start
When things were promised on calls and you need each one listed with an owner and proof
Each week, to spot promises that clash and those not yet proved delivered
When the buyer's sponsor needs a one-page weekly note on progress and blockers

tasks.task: Write the end-of-pilot readout and decision memo

items.when: When the pilot has ended and the sponsor needs a short memo to forward to the approver
When the pilot was of an AI feature and results must be read against a baseline
When you want a second one-page version with the answer and numbers first, to compare
When pilot results must be scaled to a low, base and high yearly figure with assumptions
Before the memo goes, so each result traces to pilot data with a date

tasks.task: Write a solution design summary for the buyer's team

items.when: When the buyer's IT team needs what will be set up, how it connects and what they must do
When there is more than one way to fit their systems and the trade-offs must be shown
When the summary needs a data flow or system diagram the buyer can paste into their docs
When the summary will also be read by the business sponsor and the terms lose them
Before it goes, to catch term clashes, typos and jargon

tasks.task: Answer technical objections honestly

items.when: When a buyer raises one objection and the rep needs a true answer fast
When you need the full sheet of likely objections with an honest answer to each
When you want the toughest objections found and answered a second way, with limits admitted
When you paste what the buyer said and need what sits behind it and proof to use
Before an answer is reused, to find any line that claims more than the product does

tasks.task: Answer a security or vendor questionnaire from evidence

items.when: When a questionnaire arrives and every answer must come from the seller's own evidence
When you need a sourced draft, an evidence index and the questions others must answer
Before saying a standard is met, to see the gaps against it and what proof an auditor wants
When the buyer asks about a framework and you need its evidence list with gaps ranked
Before sending, so every yes points to a dated policy, report or record
When an answer names a control but not what it protects or what it leaves open

tasks.task: Run a security review from request to buyer approval

items.when: When a buyer asks for your security documents or sends a form with a deadline
When the review will take several rounds and each step needs an owner
When you must gather the evidence pack: an index, a gap list and who supplies what by when
When some evidence has expired or is missing and each owner needs a request
When the buyer asks for a SOC 2 report the seller does not yet have

tasks.task: Write the technical sections of an RFP response

items.when: When the RFP has technical questions that must be answered from what the product does today
Before writing, to sort requirements into must-have and scored and see where you are weak
When you want a second outline showing which win theme each technical section carries
When an answer is over the word limit
Before the answers go to the bid lead, to see which claims lack proof or go too far

tasks.task: Score requirement fit and compare with a rival

items.when: When the buyer sends a requirement list and you need a gap score and a rival feature table
When you have facts on a rival and need their features and limits set against yours
When the buyer asks for a side-by-side they can show their team
When the technical card on a rival may be out of date after their last release
Before a comparison leaves, so each statement about the rival has a dated public source

tasks.task: Answer integration, migration and sizing questions

items.when: When the buyer asks how the product fits their stack and you must show options and trade-offs
When they ask if it will handle their volume and what still needs a load test
When they ask how their data moves across without a break in service
When the design crosses the buyer's network and the trust boundaries need drawing

tasks.task: Answer privacy and data handling questions

items.when: When the privacy questions sit inside a wider questionnaire
When a buyer asks how customer data is used and you need the duties and proof that apply
When the buyer sends a data processing agreement and you need each term checked first
When the buyer asks about AI features, to see how your own terms read on training and liability

tasks.task: Explain the technology to non-technical buyers

items.when: When a concept needs an everyday comparison, with where the comparison breaks down
When words alone are not landing, to plan a diagram that pairs with them
When a small visual with sliders would let the buyer see the effect for themselves
When the explanation is written, to find jargon the finance lead will not know
When you cannot explain it without the product's own vocabulary

tasks.task: Prepare demo data and a recorded walkthrough

items.when: When the demo needs realistic fake data shaped like the buyer's industry
When the demo environment must be reloaded with the same data before every run
When people who missed the demo need a short walkthrough video or GIF
When a recorded demo needs trimming and captions before it is shared

tasks.task: Plan the technical evaluation for one deal

items.when: When a qualified deal needs its demo, pilot and decision steps set out with owners
When you need the deal's risks ranked and the gaps on the technical side named
When the buyer's team should share a dated plan to their decision
When a rival is also in evaluation and the plan must answer them

tasks.task: Build the numbers for the buyer's business case

items.when: When the gain must be shown as low, base and high with each assumption listed
When the buyer's finance team will ask for payback, return and risk
Before the workbook goes to the buyer, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Hand the deal over to the delivery team after the win

items.when: When the handover should start from the solution summary the buyer already agreed
When the delivery lead needs a note they can run from on day one
When the signed customer needs onboarding stages, owners and checks to first value
Before handing over, to list every promise made in the sale so none is lost

tasks.task: Keep a technical answer bank up to date

items.when: When answers from the last questionnaire should be saved with their evidence for reuse
When stored answers cite reports, versions or certificates that may have run out
When nobody knows where answers live or who keeps them fresh

always.when: Before anything technical goes to a buyer, so each claim has a dated source or is cut
Before a document leaves, to catch typos and a feature named two ways

helpers.when: When a questionnaire exposes a real control gap that must be fixed before you can answer
When the buyer needs audit evidence or a framework mapping the seller has not prepared
When the technical answers sit inside a full tender with a compliance matrix and deadlines
When the buyer's integration needs a real design, not a summary
When the buyer needs set-up guides or API documents as part of the evaluation
When the pilot is won and onboarding and adoption must be planned

gaps: No library item turns discovery notes into a tailored demo script; only general demo scripts exist
No library item checks discovery notes for what is missing before a demo is built
No library item writes an end-of-pilot readout and decision memo for a pilot that is not about AI
No library item answers standard forms such as the CSA CAIQ or the SIG by question id from an evidence library
No library item builds a trust pack: which security documents to send, in what order and under what terms
No library item answers a buyer's AI questionnaire on models, training data and human review
No library item writes a solution design summary for a buyer's IT team
No library item scopes implementation effort so the quote matches the solution
No library item plans a demo environment: reset steps, fallbacks when a feature fails, and a dry run
No library item makes two or three clearly different demo storylines to compare
